comment: At 1920 by 1080. A 2048 by 1024 latitude and longitude grid is imported and assigned equirectangular in Blender's orientation, a Paint layer is added above it and P turns the Environment view on at yaw nought, where the view's uncovered frame is 1220 by 992 about the window point (990, 560) at a field of view of 75 degrees. A magenta brush stroke runs along the horizon from the view's left at x 400 to x 1590, ten short of its right edge where the Layers docker starts, and the texel reads find it at the document pixels the camera's rays give, worked out from the angles as x = (atan((sx - 990) * 2 tan 37.5 / 992) / TAU + 0.25) * 2048 on row 512: 271 at x 400, 301 at 500, 375 at 700, 512 at 990, 658 at 1300, 730 at 1500 and 755 at 1590, with none forty pixels above or below the row, none at the 1544 the flat view's pan and zoom would give for x 1300, and none in the canvas's middle. A drag of 1015 pixels to the right with the pan tool turns the camera ninety degrees left to face the seam, and a cyan stroke from x 690 to 1290 across the middle lands from 1907 through the right edge and on from the left edge to 142, read either side of the seam with none in the canvas's middle. The seam is drawn as one with the red meridian either side of it, a cell's width of the whole canvas no longer drawn there. P again shows the flat picture with both strokes where they landed and the seam's guide at the left and right edges. Last, a grey 1024 by 512 document fitted flat shows no guide, and the same document assigned equirectangular shows it at both edges.
